summary: This Dockerfile creates an Ubuntu container with git and git-delta (a syntax-aware diff tool) pre-installed and configured. It sets up a demo git repository with a JavaScript file and an uncommitted change, then configures the shell prompt to show a whale emoji so you know you're inside a container.

explanations.3: This tells the installer (apt-get) to run without asking interactive questions, which is necessary in Docker since there's no user to answer prompts.
explanations.7: Ubuntu's default package sources don't include 'universe' and 'multiverse' repositories, so this line edits the sources list file to add them so we can find git-delta.
explanations.13: After installing packages, this deletes the cached package lists to shrink the final image size — Docker images are smaller when you clean up after installation.
explanations.16: These git config commands set delta as the default tool for showing diffs and customize how it looks (side-by-side, with line numbers, etc.).
explanations.29: This chains commands together: create a directory, change into it, then continue with git setup — the && means each command only runs if the previous one succeeded.
explanations.30: git init -q creates a new git repository in that directory; the -q flag means quiet (no verbose output).
explanations.31: This writes a sample JavaScript function to a file using printf; the \n are newline characters to make the code readable.
explanations.34: This modifies the file we just committed, so now git diff will show a real change — the file has been edited but not yet staged or committed.
explanations.39: This appends a custom shell prompt to the bashrc file; the \e codes are terminal color escape sequences, and \$(whoami) will expand to show the current user.
explanations.41: CMD tells Docker what to run by default when the container starts — in this case, an interactive bash shell.
